title: Characteristics of a good silage
text:
Characteristics of a good silage:

CHARACTERISTICS | GOOD SILAGE | BAD SILAGE
Color | Bright, light green yellow or green brown | Dark green to Dark brown
Texture | When tightly squeezing the silage: it breaks slowly into two. | If very low moisture: the silage breaks into small pieces. / If moisture is too high: water is dripping
Oder | Sweet-Sour pleasant smell | Manure smell or putrid smell

Feeding silage to dairy cattle:
• Slowly introduce the silage to the animals.
• After feeding silage, the feed bunks must be cleaned out to prevent any remaining silage to spoil and cause contamination to the next feed out.
• Cover or seal the silage after use to prevent spoilage.

facts: Good silage has a bright, light green yellow or green brown color.
Bad silage has a dark green to dark brown color.
When tightly squeezing good silage, it breaks slowly into two.
If silage has very low moisture, it breaks into small pieces when squeezed.
If silage moisture is too high, water drips from it when squeezed.
Good silage has a sweet-sour pleasant odor or smell.
Bad silage has a manure smell or putrid smell.
Silage should be slowly introduced to dairy cattle.
Feed bunks must be cleaned out after feeding silage to prevent remaining silage from spoiling and contaminating the next feed out.
Silage must be covered or sealed after use to prevent spoilage.

questions.question: What is the expected color of high-quality (good) silage?

options.A: Bright, light green yellow or green brown
options.C: Deep jet black with white mold
options.D: Bright golden orange to pale white

questions.question: How should good silage behave when tightly squeezed by hand?

options.A: It crumbles instantly into a fine powder
options.C: Water drips continuously from the palm
options.D: It shatters into numerous small pieces

questions.question: If water drips when silage is tightly squeezed, what does this indicate about the silage?

options.A: The moisture content is too low
options.B: The silage has perfect lactic fermentation
options.C: The moisture content is too high
options.D: The silage has optimal dry matter content

questions.question: What happens when silage with very low moisture is tightly squeezed?

options.A: It breaks slowly into two sections
options.D: It forms a dense, unbreakable ball

questions.question: Which of the following describes the typical odor of properly fermented, good silage?
Which of the following statements regarding bad silage characteristics is TRUE?

options.A: Bad silage is bright, light green yellow and smells sweet-sour.
options.B: Bad silage exhibits a manure smell or putrid smell.
options.C: Bad silage breaks slowly into two when squeezed tightly.
options.D: Bad silage never displays dark green to dark brown coloration.

questions.question: How should silage initially be introduced into dairy cattle rations?

options.A: Quickly in full daily ration amounts on day one
options.B: Only as a liquid slurry mixed with molasses
options.D: After boiling and drying in full sun for two days

questions.question: Why must feed bunks be thoroughly cleaned out after feeding silage to dairy cattle?

options.A: To lower the bunk surface temperature for cattle resting
options.B: To prevent remaining silage from spoiling and contaminating the next feed out
options.C: To collect uneaten silage for re-ensiling in the bunker
options.D: To increase the ruminal pH of cows during feeding

questions.question: What essential maintenance step should be done after taking silage from storage for daily use?

options.A: Cover or seal the silage after use to prevent spoilage
options.B: Aerate the remaining silage with electric blowers
options.C: Spray excess water over the exposed silage face
options.D: Leave the silage pit uncovered to let air circulate freely
